title: Heuristic prefilter + progressive early-stop rerank pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our reranking endpoint is frequently the dominant contributor to tail latency for multi-stage search flows when candidate sets are large (>200). Current server-side batching and token-limits reduce cost but still allocate full model work for many low-quality candidates. Goal: reduce median and tail latency for rerank while keeping quality loss <1% on NDCG@10 for core ecom and qa workloads. Approach: introduce a two-stage progressive pipeline: 1) a very cheap heuristic prefilter that computes a lightweight score for each candidate (options: sparse lexical overlap, 64-d embedding sketch from a smaller model, or token-length heuristics) to drop ~60-80% of candidates before heavy scoring; 2) a progressive reranker that scores remaining candidates in priority-ordered micro-batches with an early-stop criterion (score delta threshold + confidence interval) and soft timeouts per-request. This allows parallelization across micro-batches, aggressive token limits for low-priority batches, and selective KV-cache prefetching for high-confidence candidates. Design details: - Prefilter: implement an option in the rerank API to run prefilter mode. Default strategy: cheap embedding sketch produced by the off-the-shelf 8-bit distilled embedder (embed-mini-64) + cosine threshold. Fallback to lexical overlap if embed service unavailable. - Progressive scorer: reorganize server pipeline to accept ordered candidate queues with priority tags (high/medium/low). Use a micro-batch size of 8 for high priority, 16 for medium, 32 for low; each micro-batch has a soft deadline derived from request SLO and remaining budget. Implement early-stop when the top-K candidate scores have not changed beyond delta=0.02 for two consecutive micro-batches. - Parallelism: allow concurrent scoring lanes (up to 3) per request pinned to separate GPU streams; implement lightweight admission control to avoid interfering with throughput SLOs. - Token limits and KV policy: impose per-batch token caps based on priority; enable partial KV warmup for high-priority candidates only. - Timeouts: soft per-batch timeouts that trigger fallback ranking (e.g., return best-so-far) rather than hard aborts. - Telemetry: add metrics for prefilter drop rate, early-stop triggers, per-priority latency histograms, quality delta (NDCG change) per request cohort. Success metrics: - Median rerank latency reduced by >=25% on large candidate sets (>=200). - P99 rerank latency reduced by >=30% without increasing end-to-end error rate. - NDCG@10 regression <1% on evaluation workloads. Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged internal beta (small shard) running prefilter + progressive scorer with logging only. 2) A/B experiment on 5% production traffic for two weeks with close monitoring of quality metrics. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% with dynamic fallback if quality drift observed. API changes: - Add query param rerank_mode with values [full, prefilter+progressive] and rerank_options JSON-encoded in request metadata (priority hints, time_budget_ms). Implementation notes: - We'll add a new scheduling component in the serving layer to orchestrate micro-batches and concurrency lanes. - Prefilter should be implemented as a thin call to the embedding service; circuit breaker required. - Provide a console dashboard with prefilter statistics and early-stop counters. Trade-offs: - Extra complexity in scheduler and more telemetry to maintain. - Slightly more CPU and embedding service usage for prefilter stage, but net GPU token reduction is expected. - Risk of quality regressions for adversarial candidate lists; mitigate via conservative thresholds and staged rollouts. Tests and validation: - Offline: run end-to-end batch experiments across benchmark sets (ecom, faq, longform) measuring NDCG, MRR, latency/cost. - Perf: microbenchmarks for lane concurrency and soft timeouts. - Integration: canary + rollback automation. PRs & artifacts: design doc and perf scripts in Drive + initial implementation PRs under github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service.
acceptance_criteria: Prefilter integration is optional and off by default behind a feature flag
Median and P99 improvements meet targets on staging benchmarks
No manual quality regressions >1% NDCG on evaluation suites
Production telemetry with prefilter drop rate and early-stop counters visible in console
Automated canary rollback if quality drift >0.5% observed during A/B
